name: Kejia Wang

attribution.legal_posture: Convicted by guilty plea and sentenced; the exact criminal docket is D. Mass. No. 1:25-cr-10274-NMG; U.S. laptop-farm and money-laundering facilitator.

caveats: The information is a charging instrument; the later judgment and DOJ release establish the adjudicated posture.

sources.support: The filed information identifies United States v. Kejia Wang, D. Mass. No. 1:25-cr-10274-NMG
sources.locator: D. Mass. No. 1:25-cr-10274-NMG, Doc. 1, caption and paragraphs 7-8

sources.support: The final judgment identifies Kejia Wang's criminal docket and adjudicated disposition

DOJ names Kejia Wang in the coordinated nationwide action. The release-wide laptop-farm, account, website, and separate virtual-currency-case totals are aggregate context, not conduct attributed to him individually.
sources.locator: Named Kejia Wang paragraph and release-wide scheme summary

sources.support: DOJ reports Kejia Wang’s guilty plea and 108-month sentence; his U.S.-based management role; and the defendants’ joint creation of three shell companies and related financial accounts. The release attributes unauthorized access to ITAR-controlled data to an overseas co-conspirator, not personally to Kejia Wang.

sources.quote: Kejia Wang went on to serve as the U.S.-based manager for the scheme, supervising at least five facilitators in the United States who collectively hosted hundreds of computers of U.S. victim companies at their residences.

notes: DOJ's post-sentencing description; victim and residence details are not separately retained.

sources.quote: Kejia Wang traveled to Shenyang and Dandong, China on two separate occasions in 2023, to meet with overseas actors about the scheme, including a former classmate that Kejia Wang knew was from North Korea.

notes: This records source-reported travel, not residence or current location.

sources.quote: On or about February 18, 2022, KEJIA WANG registered Tony WKJ LLC

notes: The source is an information; the organizational act is therefore retained with high rather than confirmed confidence.

sources.locator: Paragraph beginning “Kejia Wang and Zhenxing Wang created shell companies”
sources.quote: Kejia Wang and Zhenxing Wang created shell companies with corresponding financial accounts, including Hopana Tech LLC, Tony WKJ LLC, and Independent Lab LLC, to make it appear as though the overseas IT workers were affiliated with legitimate U.S. businesses.

notes: This is a joint act; Independent Lab LLC is not attributed to Kejia Wang alone.

sources.locator: Section “The Tony Wang Link,” first paragraph
sources.quote: HopanaTech’s website, hopanatech[.]com, listed three contacts before it was taken down by law enforcement. The first person, Wang Kejia, is listed with the email address “Tonywkj”.

notes: Historical third-party observation only. It does not establish current account ownership, control of the website, or a separate natural person; the email address itself is deliberately not retained.

identity_boundary: Kejia Wang, also named Tony Wang in the captioned federal case; keep adjudicated facts separate from allegations in the information and from historical website labels or company personas.
